The Hecke algebra is a quotient of the braid group on $n$ strands, which is defined by removing relation [\[eqn:hecke1\]](#eqn:hecke1){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:hecke1"}. Specifically, the braid group is generated by $\sigma_1^{\pm 1},...,\sigma_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ modulo relations [\[eqn:hecke2\]](#eqn:hecke2){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:hecke2"} and [\[eqn:hecke3\]](#eqn:hecke3){reference-type="eqref" reference="eqn:hecke3"}. By definition, the **full twist** on $n$ strands is the braid: $$\mathbf{FT}_n = (\sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{n-1})^{n}.$$

Examples
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:exprojectors label="sec:exprojectors"}

In this subsection, we use the local geometry of the flag Hilbert scheme to describe the homology of categorified projectors on two and three strands.

::: example
For the $S^2$ projector, we have $$Y=\left(\begin{matrix}
0 & 0\\
1 & 0\\
\end{matrix}\right).$$ The commutation relation implies that $X$ is of the form $$X=\left(\begin{matrix}
u_1 & 0\\
u_2 & u_1\\
\end{matrix}\right).$$ One has $\deg(u_1)=q$, $\deg(u_2)=q/t$, so the Poincaré series equals $$P(\mathring{\mathcal{A}}_T)=\frac{1}{(1-q)(1-q/t)}.$$
:::

Dg schemes can be defined as spectra of dg algebras with respect to the étale topology, as detailed in [@B]. We will not need the full theory, and instead follow the original definition of Kontsevich.

:::
